newsitem.title: USA: Oregon, tribe reach pact to hold casino expansion.
newsitem.headline: Oregon, tribe reach pact to hold casino expansion.

text.p: The state of Oregon and the Confederated Tribes of the Grand Ronde signed a pact Friday that will limit the tribe to one casino and require it to contribute profits to community programs, the state said.
The agreement limits the Grand Ronde tribe to owning and operating only one casino, Spirit Mountain Casino, in the remote community of Grand Ronde about 60 miles from Portland.

The agreement also established a community benefit fund equal to six percent of the casino's net revenues to help finance education, health and public safety programs. The fund would contain about $1.6 million for 1997, officials said.
The state said the pact would allow the tribe to offer a wider variety of gaming.
Oregon Gov. John Kitzhaber said the agreement was the first of its kind in the state and set a new standard of cooperation between the state and tribal governments.

"This compact allows us to accomplish one of our main objectives with regards to tribal gaming in Oregon," said Kitzhaber. "This is an important step toward ensuring that there is not a proliferation of tribal casinos throughout the state."
Spirit Mountain Casino, which opened in October 1995, currently employs 1,050 people. The casino said it would generate about $25 million in profits this year.
